title: OpenCl compiling issue
body: I'm trying to compile llama.cpp with OpenCL on a Samsung S10+ using Termux. Running make with LAMA_CLBLAST=1 fails because ggml-opencl.cpp cannot find clblast.h. My Termux include path is /data/data/com.termux/files/usr/include, so I tried replacing <clblast.h> with ocl_icd.h, but the build then fails with an undeclared identifier 'clblast'.

symptoms_visible: Running make with LAMA_CLBLAST=1 on my Samsung S10+ in Termux stops at 'fatal error: clblast.h file not found'.
After I replaced clblast.h with ocl_icd.h, compilation reaches ggml-opencl.cpp but stops with "use of undeclared identifier 'clblast'".
N0.label: N0 make build cannot use CLBlast

symptoms_visible: The CMake build appears to complete, but running ./main from the source directory says the command is not found.
N1.label: N1 CMake build produced binary elsewhere

symptoms_visible: I can run ./main from the build bin subdirectory, but startup does not show a CLBlast platform or device.
Configuring with -DLLAMA_CLBLAST=ON prints 'CLBlast not found' and says it cannot find CLBlastConfig.cmake or clblast-config.cmake.
N2.label: N2 CLBlast package configuration missing

symptoms_visible: After installing CLBlast into the Termux prefix, llama.cpp finds it and builds with CLBlast enabled.
When I run ./main, the OpenCL program emits errors including '16-bit storage is not supported for SSBOs', '8-bit storage is not supported for SSBOs', and alignment errors.
N3.label: N3 CLBlast builds but clvk runtime fails

symptoms_visible: With the Termux clvk platform, clpeak identifies an Adreno 640 through 'CLVK on Vulkan' and prints 'No half precision support! Skipped'.
The CLBlast-enabled executable still emits OpenCL kernel compilation errors at startup.
N4.label: N4 clvk capabilities measured

symptoms_visible: A manually built clinfo sees one native 'QUALCOMM Snapdragon(TM)' OpenCL 2.0 platform and an Adreno 640 device.
The native device information lists half support with cl_khr_fp16.
N5.label: N5 native Qualcomm OpenCL discovered

symptoms_visible: My native Qualcomm OpenCL platform reports cl_khr_fp16 support, while the earlier no-half result came from the clvk platform.
The CLBlast-enabled program still needs access to the native vendor OpenCL library when launched from Termux.
N5_x.label: N5_x no-half incompatibility conclusion rejected

symptoms_visible: After a fresh Termux setup, rebuilding CLBlast and llama.cpp, and launching main with /vendor/lib64 and the Termux library directory in LD_LIBRARY_PATH, llama.cpp starts with CLBlast GPU acceleration enabled.
N_terminal.label: terminal CLBlast GPU acceleration works

solution.intent: Stop substituting an unrelated OpenCL ICD header for the CLBlast API and use the project's CMake build so dependencies can be discovered and configured correctly.
solution.concrete_example: Restore #include <clblast.h>, create a CMake build with cmake -B build, and compile it with cmake --build build or make from the build directory.

edges.comment: The initial source edit substituted the ICD loader header for CLBlast's distinct API and could not declare the clblast namespace. CMake successfully produced a build, but the first build did not yet contain CLBlast.

question_patterns: Run CMake with -DLLAMA_CLBLAST=ON and paste the CLBlast-related configuration output.
Does CMake find CLBlast when you explicitly enable LLAMA_CLBLAST?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I ran cmake . -DLLAMA_CLBLAST=ON. It warns 'CLBlast not found' and says it cannot find CLBlastConfig.cmake or clblast-config.cmake.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: CMake reports that CLBlast was found, and startup names an OpenCL platform and device.
The same missing CLBlast package-config warning appears from a separate build directory.

solution.intent: Run the CMake-built executable from build/bin and explicitly enable the CLBlast backend during configuration.
solution.concrete_example: Configure with cmake -B build -DLLAMA_CLBLAST=ON, build it, and run ./build/bin/main; CMake builds place main under the build directory's bin subdirectory.
solution.inference_hint: The lack of a CLBlast platform/device message and BLAS indication means the first successful CMake build did not include CLBlast.

edges.comment: The binary-location question and the missing backend were separate consequences of the CMake build. The CLBlast warning establishes that the development package/configuration is absent, rather than showing a llama.cpp source error.

solution.intent: Install the Termux OpenCL development dependencies, build CLBlast itself, install it under the Termux prefix using CMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX, and then rebuild llama.cpp with CLBlast enabled.
solution.concrete_example: Install clang, cmake, opencl-headers and ocl-icd; clone CLBlast; configure it with -DBUILD_SHARED_LIBS=OFF -DTUNERS=OFF -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DCMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX=/data/data/com.termux/files/usr; run make and make install; then configure llama.cpp with cmake -B build -DLLAMA_CLBLAST=ON and build it.

edges.comment: CLBlast_DIR must refer to CLBlast's CMake package files, not the OpenCL headers. The reporter initially confused CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH with CMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX and hit an attempted /usr/local/lib installation; correcting the install-prefix variable allowed both projects to build.

question_patterns: Which OpenCL platform is the program using, and what does clpeak report about its numeric capabilities?
Please run clpeak and paste the platform, device, and half-precision result.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: clpeak reports driver '3.0 CLVK on Vulkan' on my Adreno GPU. It prints float benchmarks, then says 'No half precision support! Skipped' and 'No double precision support! Skipped'.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: clpeak is using the native Qualcomm OpenCL platform and reports cl_khr_fp16 support without kernel compilation errors.
The clvk benchmark scores differ, but it still reports no half-precision support.

edges.comment: This is a capability probe. The answer is the raw clpeak output; deciding whether the device or only the clvk translation layer is incompatible remains engineer-side.

question_patterns: Can you check whether the phone exposes a native OpenCL platform instead of clvk, for example by manually building clinfo against the vendor libraries?
What does clinfo report when it accesses the phone's native Qualcomm OpenCL driver?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I manually built clinfo. It sees one platform named 'QUALCOMM Snapdragon(TM)', OpenCL 2.0, and one 'QUALCOMM Adreno(TM) 640' GPU. The output lists native half size 1 and half-precision support through cl_khr_fp16.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The native check also reports zero platforms, so only the clvk package exposes an OpenCL device.
The same Qualcomm OpenCL 2.0 platform and cl_khr_fp16 support appear with a slightly different driver build identifier.

edges.comment: The manually built clinfo probe distinguishes the phone's native Qualcomm OpenCL implementation from Termux's experimental clvk-on-Vulkan platform.

solution.intent: Conclude that the Samsung device cannot run llama.cpp with CLBlast because clpeak under clvk says half precision is unsupported.
solution.concrete_example: The phone cannot support llama.cpp's OpenCL backend because the clvk clpeak output says there is no half precision support; use CPU/OpenBLAS only.

edges.comment: This conclusion was corrected in the thread. Half precision is not universally required in the claimed way, and the reporter's native Qualcomm clinfo output explicitly reports cl_khr_fp16. The failing capability report came from clvk, not the native vendor driver.

solution.intent: Use the native Qualcomm OpenCL driver from Termux: start from a clean package setup, install and build CLBlast into the Termux prefix, build llama.cpp with CLBlast enabled, and expose both the vendor and Termux library directories at runtime.
solution.concrete_example: On a clean Termux installation, install git, clang, cmake, make, opencl-headers, opencl-clhpp, ocl-icd and clinfo. Build and install CLBlast with CMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX=/data/data/com.termux/files/usr, rebuild llama.cpp with -DLLAMA_CLBLAST=ON, then run `LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/vendor/lib64:$PREFIX/lib ./main` from build/bin and confirm startup selects the OpenCL platform/device.
solution.inference_hint: The contrast between clvk's kernel failures and the native clinfo result shows that the phone itself is not the unsupported component. Termux must load the Qualcomm vendor library from /vendor/lib64 while retaining its own prefix library path for CLBlast and the ICD loader.

edges.comment: The reporter's final resolution used a fresh Termux setup, the corrected CLBlast install prefix, a CLBlast-enabled llama.cpp CMake build, and `LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/vendor/lib64:$PREFIX/lib ./main`. Later reports confirmed this enabled GPU acceleration, although it was slower than OpenBLAS on this phone.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify both layers of the original failure: CLBlast was not installed or discoverable by CMake, and replacing clblast.h with ocl_icd.h cannot provide the CLBlast API.

Must ground the runtime diagnosis in the collected evidence: the failing platform was experimental clvk-on-Vulkan, while manually built clinfo found the native Qualcomm OpenCL 2.0 Adreno 640 driver with cl_khr_fp16 support.
Must not conclude that the phone is inherently incompatible merely because clpeak under clvk reports no half-precision support; that conclusion was falsified by the native driver evidence.

The working setup must install CLBlast under the Termux prefix with CMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX, build llama.cpp with LLAMA_CLBLAST=ON, and launch with both /vendor/lib64 and $PREFIX/lib available through LD_LIBRARY_PATH.
Must ask the user to verify that the rebuilt executable starts and reports the OpenCL platform/device before treating GPU acceleration as resolved.

persona_hint.experience_level: Persistent but relatively inexperienced command-line user. Can clone repositories, run CMake and make, edit cache files, install Termux packages, and paste extensive compiler or capability output, but needs precise path and build-variable instructions.
persona_hint.communication_style: Polite, appreciative, and highly cooperative; provides long raw logs, explains attempted changes, asks for explicit step-by-step directions, and follows up with a tested resolution for other Termux users.
